brief_rationale: The doctor fulfilled all responsibility chain items across the preoperative, operative, and post-discharge phases, achieving safe medication management, red flag education, fall prevention, and teach-back verification. Four high-order points were completed: HO2 (false-positive verification distinguishing confirmed vs. unconfirmed findings), HO3 (repairing family conflict about mobilization), HO4 (safe bounded closure with clear residual uncertainty), and HO1 (red flag prioritization with emergency pathway). The trajectory demonstrates excellent continuity, actionability, and clinical reasoning with verifiable family teach-back.

closure_assessment.explanation: The trajectory concludes with a complete, verifiable teach-back where the family accurately restates medication dosing, wound care, mobilization limits, and red flag actions. The doctor confirmed all points and provided a structured four-point home instruction list. Residual uncertainties (follow-up timing, rehabilitation progression) are appropriately deferred to the scheduled clinical visits with clear responsibility assignment.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The family initially reported conflict (some urging quick mobilization, others fearing falls). The doctor repaired this by establishing a single, medically-supervised mobilization protocol: all transfers require nurse/rehab therapist evaluation and assistance, neither self-imposed bed rest nor unsupervised ambulation.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The doctor achieved bounded closure by clearly partitioning: (1) immediately executable home actions - medication dosing, wound care, fall prevention, red flag recognition; (2) deferred decisions requiring clinical reassessment - anticoagulation duration, rehabilitation progression, suture removal timing. This prevents premature closure on unresolved medical decisions while ensuring all current-phase safety actions are actionable.
